audit.whatIsWrong: Hookshot's cooldown was written as 11 seconds at level 1 and the Levels 4-5 stage gave no number at all.
audit.why: Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12s — 16 at rank 1, 13 by rank 4. An eleven-second belief means walking into a live Hookshot every lap.
audit.corrected: early corrected to 16 seconds; phases[3].why now gives 13s at rank 4 and the wall-proximity rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry calls Tactical Sweep a 'true-damage cone' in five places and tells you to fear the centre of it. It also calls Hookshot a stun.
audit.why: Riot's text: Tactical Sweep blasts a cone after a delay; enemies in the OUTER half are slowed, take extra damage, and heal Camille. The true damage in her kit is on Precision Protocol (Q), not W. And Hookshot knocks up on landing — it is a knockup, not a stun. Standing in the inner half is the actual counterplay and the entry told you the opposite.
audit.corrected: whys[2], spikes[1], wants.you[1], wants.foe[0], wants.foe[2] and early restated: outer edge is the damage-and-heal half, inner half is where you want to be; Hookshot knocks up; Precision Protocol carries the true damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds timing despite Tactical Sweep healing her every time the outer edge lands.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags needs-antiheal on Tactical Sweep, and this entry's own plan is to force extended trades after Heartsteel — the exact fights her healing decides.
audit.corrected: late now puts the anti-heal buy ahead of the long trade.

edits.before: Level 1 is the one stage where neither kit has a decisive edge — her Q true-damage procs off autos but her E hookshot is on a long cooldown at 11 seconds, so she cannot chain-stun you freely. The moment you hit level 2, W-shield changes the math: start a trade by baiting her into auto range, pop W to eat her first Q proc, then charge your Q while her hookshot is on cooldown. She cannot safely E into you while your Q is charging without eating the full knockup. At level 3 she has her full kit and her W true-damage cone becomes the real threat — never let her land both Q autos plus a centered W cone in the same trade or she will shred 15–20% of your max HP in one exchange.
edits.after: Level 1 is the one stage where neither kit has a decisive edge — Precision Protocol procs true damage off her autos, but Hookshot is 16 seconds at rank 1, so she cannot chain-knock you up freely. The moment you hit level 2, Soul Furnace changes the math: bait her into auto range, pop W to eat her first Q proc, then charge your Q while Hookshot is on cooldown. She cannot safely E into you mid-charge without eating the full knockup. At level 3 Tactical Sweep becomes the real threat — never let her land both Q autos plus the outer edge of that cone in one trade, because the outer half also heals her back up.

edits.before: First item Heartsteel flips the math back in your favor — your HP total starts punishing her Q true-damage scaling (her Q procs deal a flat percent, but your zombie passive threat compounds exponentially with HP). Force trades on hookshot's cooldown the moment Heartsteel completes: E armor-shred first to drop her resistances, then commit the charged Q knockup. At two items your W-shield absorbs most of her damage budget in a single trade, and your passive zombie form means any dive attempt by Camille ends with her taking damage from a rampaging corpse she cannot safely ignore. She still wins if she catches you isolated with both your W and R on cooldown, so never over-extend in the side-lane without those available.
edits.after: First item Heartsteel flips the math back in your favor — your HP total outgrows her burst budget (your zombie threat compounds with HP). Buy Grievous Wounds before you commit to any long trade, or Tactical Sweep's outer edge refunds what you chip. Force trades on Hookshot's cooldown the moment Heartsteel completes: Roar of the Slayer's armour shred first, then the charged Q knockup. At two items Soul Furnace absorbs most of her damage in a single trade, and your zombie form means any dive attempt ends with her taking damage from a corpse she cannot ignore. She still wins if she catches you isolated with W and R down, so never over-extend in the side lane without those available.

notes: Biggest correction: Tactical Sweep is not a true-damage cone and its OUTER half is the dangerous, self-healing half — the entry told you to fear the centre, which is backwards. True damage lives on Precision Protocol. Hookshot knocks up rather than stuns and is 16s at rank 1, not 11. Chart flipped to the packet shape as matched pairs, with the affected ratings moved with it. I did NOT write the missingInteractions claims that The Hextech Ultimatum is an interruptible channel or grants untargetability: Riot's own description says only that she dashes to the target and anchors them, and the brief warns derived flags misfire — recorded as unverified rather than shipped.
